notes: Summary: RidgePoint is a mid-market product-analytics SaaS evaluating Redwood after a 3-week Hosted API trial. Primary goal: move to Dedicated for predictable latency/cost and VPC isolation.
Trial scope: chat-based support assistant + doc-search reranker + summarization endpoint. Traffic mirrored from prod staging to Hosted API; ~150k requests during test window.

Observed baseline metrics (Hosted API, model: redwood-compat-13b-quant): avg QPS=6 sustained, median concurrency=4, peak observed QPS=48 (10-minute spike), peak concurrency=60 (bursting from scheduled report jobs).
Token mix (measured): 70% short requests (avg 120 tokens), 25% medium (avg 420 tokens), 5% long (avg 1,500 tokens). Weighted avg tokens/request ~235 tokens.
Monthly extrapolation (product team forecast + trial uplift): projected monthly requests 1.8M -> projected monthly tokens ~423M (sensitivity +/-25%).
Latency targets: product wants p50 <= 120ms for short chat turns, p95 <= 400ms across all requests. Hosted p95 averaged 320ms for short, 780ms for long requests (long requests skew latency).

Quality tradeoffs: they prefer deterministic outputs for support agent (lower temp, system prompts) and higher creativity for summarization. Will accept quantized models if quality delta <6% on eval set.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market deal; willing to commit to a 12-month reserved capacity if ~20-30% discount vs on-demand Hosted token economics; target ARR $90k-$120k.

POC learnings: prefix caching on doc-search reduced tokens served by ~18% for repeat queries; batching helped throughput but increased p95 by ~60ms on short turns — acceptable within SLO for non-interactive endpoints.
Dedicated sizing recommendation (initial): reserve a baseline pool sized for steady-state and autoscale for peaks.

- Baseline: 3 x H100-equivalent nodes (or 4 x A100-80GB) configured for redwood-compat-13b-quant model family. Estimated steady throughput: ~20-28 QPS aggregate for chat with concurrency headroom 40-50 (assumes continuous batching & KV cache enabled).
- Burst/Autoscale: allow autoscale up to 6 nodes during predictable nightly report windows and product launches (covers observed peak QPS ~48 with buffer).
- Concurrency guidance: plan for 60 concurrent sessions total across pool (session pinning for chat KV cache helps keep token cost down).

- Token/throughput example: with quantized 13B, expect ~24 QPS per H100-equivalent for short-chat workload; long requests reduce per-GPU QPS by ~60% — recommend route long-form summarization to a specialized, lower-cost pool or schedule async jobs.

Operations: suggest 2 routing classes — interactive (low-latency chat) and batch/async (summarization, heavy reranks). Interactive routed to baseline reserved pool; batch to burstable pool with higher batching and relaxed latency SLO.

Security/Onboarding checklist: VPC peering, SAML SSO integration for admin console, KMS key wrap for model logs, audit log retention policy (30/90 days choices requested). Security team flagged DLP controls on user transcripts -> follow-up questionnaire sent.

Open items from SE call: need per-token cost estimates for reserved profile vs on-demand; request model-variant fallback plan (if dedicated capacity overloaded) and cold-start penalty estimates for autoscale events.
Finance asks: simple 12-mo commit pricing + overage rates; sample amortized per-1k tokens price and per-GPU monthly charge for reference in procurement packet.

Proposed next steps: SE to deliver final capacity spec + draft SOW by 2026-03-08; schedule executive procurement review w/ RidgePoint finance 2026-03-12; security team to complete questionnaire by 2026-03-10.
Quotes & artifacts: attached capacity forecast (Drive); pricing deck shared in email thread; Jira ticket INF-3421 opened for model fallback policy request.
Direct quote from VP Product on 2026-02-28 call: "We need predictable latency and a clear burn-rate before we sign — if Dedicated gets us within 25% of our cost target we can commit to 12 months."
Sales cues: likely to prefer Redwood if Dedicated delivers VPC & KMS integration without long security delays; procurement timeline depends on 3rd quote and internal finance cycle (end of Q2).
